title: SafetyPrompts: a Systematic Review of Open Datasets for Evaluating and Improving Large Language Model Safety

bias_targets.methodology: The paper conducts a systematic review of datasets that evaluate gender bias, noting that these datasets frequently use co-reference resolution tasks, autocomplete-style formats (filling masked words or finishing sentence snippets), and template-based prompt expansion.

The paper reviews datasets that measure racial bias in language models, highlighting the use of prompt templates, open-ended questions, and text completion tasks to evaluate sociodemographic disparities.

The paper catalogs existing datasets that evaluate bias related to sexual orientation, which typically utilize prompt formats like fill-in-the-blank templates and promptable multiple-choice questions.
The paper includes a review of safety datasets designed to measure religious bias through text completions and language model decision-making evaluations.

The paper systematically reviews datasets that assess broad sociodemographic biases using methods such as template approaches (combining sentence templates with identity descriptor terms), multiple-choice questions, and chat-style open-ended prompts.
